title: Second Shift
description: Waste is building up both outside the cell and from your own respiration. A passive channel won't help — you need to actively get rid of it, and you get to choose how.

narrative.intro: Same lab, a rougher patch of tissue this time. Waste concentration outside is high enough that a passive channel would let it flood in as easily as out — and your own mitochondria are adding to the pile from the inside. You've got two ways to deal with it: a peroxisome that destroys waste on-site (costs an organelle slot and a membrane connection), or a pump that ejects it at the membrane (costs only a connection). Pick your trade-off.
narrative.outro: Two different organelles solved the same problem two different ways — one spent a slot, one spent a connection. Real cells run both strategies simultaneously for exactly this reason: redundancy is cheap insurance when the alternative is dying to your own metabolic byproducts.

environment.description: Moderately toxic tissue — not enough to be instantly lethal, but enough that doing nothing loses.

goals.description: Keep internal waste at or below 5.
Keep cytoplasmic ATP at or above 2 for 8 straight ticks.

failConditions.description: Internal waste hit toxic levels — the cell is dead.
